scenario: Refraction per LDET.5.3, as SUPPRESSION rather than as an ordering key. Four things are pinned in one sequence. (1) `watched` fires once for Trig(v=1). (2) A second pump with an UNCHANGED LHS does not re-fire it — the whole claim, since without it a matching fact would fire on every pump for as long as it stayed in working memory. (3) An assert of an UNRELATED schema does not release the suppression: any assert bumps the generation and a stale refraction entry reads as absent, but nothing re-consults the entry, because the agenda is a pop loop. `other_rule` firing in that same pump is what proves the pump ran and the silence is refraction rather than a vacuously empty pump. (4) An identity update of the matched fact (v=1 is the key, n is mutable) IS a changed LHS and does release it, so `watched` fires a second time. Order is not asserted between the two rules and must not be: under the two-key model (creation timetag, terminal ordinal) their relative order is fixed by structure, and pinning it here would duplicate LDET.5.4/5.5 and make this fixture fail for a reason that has nothing to do with refraction.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope logical:
    v: Int key
    n: Int mutable

schema Other scope logical:
    k: Int key

rule watched:
    Trig
->
    log critical "watched"

rule other_rule:
    Other
->
    log critical "other"
